Breast-feeding is recommended over other types of feeding, and in infants at high risk of developing asthma (ﬁrst-degree relative
with atopy) where breast-feeding is not possible, hydrolyzed formula for a minimum of 4 months together with other preventative
measures may reduce the risk of developing asthma or wheeze in the ﬁrst year of life. Inconclusive evidence exists that growth rate
during infancy may be related to the risk of development of asthma.
Secondary Prophylactic Effects of Nutrition in Asthma
Intervention studies could not conﬁrm that supplementation with antioxidants produce clinical beneﬁts in asthma. Better pulmo-
nary function and less asthma have been observed, though, when there is higher intake of fresh fruit and vegetables and it seems to
